# testdata/ — the regression library

A synthetic twin of every byte shape in the owner's corpus (`exemplars.yaml`, 86 entries over 43 mimes) for
spec + tooling regression testing, plus the regression ontology those bytes classify under. Every
fixture is generated by a script kept beside it (see "The synthetic tier" and `synthetic/gen/COVERAGE.md`);
no private byte is in the set and nothing waits on a placement.

Tracked here: this README, `exemplars.yaml` (the manifest — file, blake3, mime, the shape it `classifies` as
where the ontology has one, the byte shape it is a `twin` of, and a neutral technical note, no personal content),
`seed.ts` (the regression instance pair, built with the tool), `ontology/` (the regression ontology a standalone
instance starts from), `passes/` (the generated forming pass of the asserted-tree PDF) and `synthetic/`.
**`instance/` is never tracked** — the pair `seed.ts` builds is gitignored at the repo root
(`/testdata/instance/`), as is `/testdata/regression/`, where private bytes once sat; nothing reads it.

### The synthetic tier

Fixtures with no private content, committed under `testdata/synthetic/` with manifest entries pointing at
them, and the script that generates each one kept under `testdata/synthetic/gen/`
(see `gen/README.md` for the tool and version behind every file). The committed bytes, not a fresh run of
a generator, are what the manifest's blake3 pins: an encoder's output drifts across tool versions even for
identical input, so
pinning a freshly-generated hash would make the manifest non-reproducible from one machine or ffmpeg/libheif
version to the next. The text formats the scripts write themselves do reproduce byte-for-byte.

### Generated twins (`synthetic/gen/`)

Every regression artifact is a *twin*: a fixture with the same shape as a private artifact of the owner's corpus
and fictional content, generated by a script kept under `synthetic/gen/` (`COVERAGE.md` there is the inventory
of shapes). `gen/plain.ts`
makes the twins whose test is classify + attest + lint (the readme, the script, the address book and cards,
the exchange file, the media manifest, the screenshot, the photograph with its Exif orientation, the clip,
the receipt). `gen/thread.ts`, `gen/mailing.ts`, `gen/novel.ts`, `gen/chat-archive.ts` and `gen/chat-export.ts`
make the full-shape twins of the thread capture, the mailing, the novel, the mailbox slice and the chat export,
each with a regression leg of its own and frozen counts. `gen/procedure.ts` makes the asserted-tree PDF, a fictional calculation procedure in the shape of a methodological tool: one content model drives both the typst source
(`procedure.typ`, rendered to `procedure.pdf` with typst 0.15.1 and its bundled fonts; `set document(date:
none)` makes the render byte-identical across runs) and the forming pass a reader stages
(`passes/<blake3>.p1.yaml`: the tree and the chrome rule, in the record's grammar), whose boxes are read back off
the rendered PDF through `pdf.words@1`. Re-rendering is re-running the script; the committed PDF is what the
manifest pins, and a changed render is a new blake3, a new pass file and a new golden, on purpose.

Every export arrives with its testimony beside it, `<file>.testimony.yaml`, in the contract's shape (spec §9.4):
`gen/testimony.ts` declares what each producer says and writes the sidecar about the committed bytes.

### The regression ontology

`ontology/` is laid out as an instance lays out its vocabularies — `corpus/forms/`, `corpus/shapes/`,
`graph/kinds/`, `graph/properties/` — and copied whole into an instance that starts from it. Forms are structure
only (a heading, a row, a post, a value); the shapes recognise the exports, pages and sheets of the set by more than
their mime (a selector, a first row, a constituent's path, a container's shape) and lay their trees out; the kinds
and properties are what an entity of them owes. A format is never a term: the tool knows its formats. `ath vocab
check` over an instance holding it is the gate (`ath/test/regression.test.ts`).

## The regression instance pair

`bun testdata/seed.ts [OUT]` builds, in `testdata/instance/` by default, a public standalone instance `reference`, a
private extension `household` built on it at a pinned commit, and the host state they share (`host/`: the local
store, the access file, the remotes a stand-in for rclone reaches). Every file in the two instances is written by an
`ath` verb — `instance init`, `ingest`, `vocab add`, `pass open|stage|sign`, `rule`, `store add` — except what an owner
authors by hand: the ontology copied in, the policies, and the instance and store ids, pinned so the pair is the same
on every machine. The records show the stages (spec §8.5): the procedure PDF is formed (readings and a tree, both
complete), the listing page and the mooring plan inside the drive export are read where an entity cites them, the
sign photograph is transcribed, the sheet and the thread are structured and stay at their projection, and the clip
lists its tracks as parts. `ath/test/seed.test.ts` builds it in-process and holds every file to the golden
`ath/test/fixtures/seed.jsonl`.
